review_question: Among surgically staged endometrial-cancer cohorts, is low-volume sentinel-node metastasis associated with recurrence compared with pathologically node-negative status?

population.description: Patients with surgically staged endometrial cancer in a cohort reporting sentinel-node pathology and follow-up

intervention_or_exposure.description: Low-volume nodal metastasis: isolated tumor cells or micrometastasis

outcome.description: Source-defined recurrence or disease-free survival event at source-reported follow-up
Source-defined disease recurrence recorded as binary events, with a secondary capture lane for source-reported time-to-event disease-free-survival effects.

targets.comparison: Low-volume sentinel-node metastasis versus pathologically node-negative status
targets.population_or_subgroup: Source-defined cohort; preserve adjuvant-treatment status and histology scope when reported

timepoint_policy.rule: Use the source-reported follow-up. Do not convert Kaplan-Meier survival percentages, disease-free survivor counts, or a review table into binary recurrence events.

candidate_capture_policy.record_scope: Capture source-supported ITC, micrometastasis, and node-negative arms separately. Preserve partial records and source-reported time-to-event effects instead of fabricating a binary contrast.

targets.quantitative_use_policy: A binary recurrence effect requires events and a denominator for both comparison groups. An adjusted time-to-event effect may be captured only with its explicitly source-reported estimate and confidence interval; it is not interchangeable with a binary risk ratio.

output_contract.effect_unit: source-reported low-volume-metastasis or node-negative outcome record

target_compatibility.reason: No existing seven-case v1 template has the same data contract.
